# The whole school budget

The voted school budget is the general fund. Every fund together spent $29,661,795 in FY2026, $3,374,321 more, and these pages show where it came from and which lines it paid.

*Generated by `scripts/build_school_all_funds.py` from the school MUNIS journal. Every figure is a posting to a school account, FY2023 to FY2026, and FY2026 is not yet closed. The pages are at /school-all-funds.*

- The general fund was voted $26,287,474 for FY2026; every fund together spent $29,661,795.
- Of $4,004,476 spent outside it, $2,401,020 was booked to no budget line.
- Special education ran past its vote every year; other funds paid the rest.

**How these figures tie to what the Town and the state printed — Reconciliation**

| | Compared with | Result |
|---|---:|---:|
| Period-13 spreadsheets, FY2023 to FY2026 | 939 accounts, 3,756 account-years | every one ties to the cent; they hold 94% to 97% of each year’s spending |
| The report’s own printed totals, FY2026 | 3,356 accounts | every one ties to the cent |
| Town report, special revenue, FY2023 | 12 funds | 9 tie to the cent; see Unspent money by fund |
| DESE End of Year report, FY2023 | 5 fund columns | 4 tie to the dollar: circuit breaker, school lunch, school choice, IDEA grants (#240); school gift fund differs by $1 |

*The first two must hold to the cent or nothing on these pages is written. The last two are other publishers’ readings of the same money, compared and shown.*

## School money in

**Outside the voted budget, school funds took in $3,407,472 in FY2025, most of it fees, lunch and grants.**

- The general fund was voted $26,287,474 for FY2026; Chapter 70 aid to the town was 35.1% of that.
  - *not known:* Chapter 70 is paid to the town, not to a school account, so it is shown beside the vote, never added to it. — closes: the town’s revenue ledger for the school appropriation, by source
- In FY2025 other funds took in $3,407,472: $1,683,842 from fees, lunch and gifts, $1,114,792 from grants.
- FY2026 grants had received $74,333 when the report was run.
  - *not known:* Most grants are paid after the money is spent, so a year’s receipts arrive late; an open year looks short. — closes: the DESE grant payment history (GEM$) for each school grant

## Budget lines, all funds

**In FY2026 other funds spent $4,004,476 beside the general fund; $2,401,020 of it sat on no budget line.**

- The general fund was voted $26,287,474 for FY2026 and spent $25,657,318; all funds together, $29,661,795.
  - *not known:* FY2026 is not yet closed in this run. These are postings to school accounts, not what the schools cost in full. — closes: the Town’s schedule of school benefits and town-side costs, by fund
- Other funds spent on 5 of the 41 voted lines; $681,445 landed on one.
  - *not known:* The largest was 9400 Tuition to Collaboratives: $333,495 from other funds. — closes: the fund-by-fund budget for each line, as the district builds it
- $2,401,020 of other-fund spending had no line: function 0000 or a heading.
  - *not known:* It is shown as its own row and not spread across lines: the ledger does not say which line it served. — closes: the district’s grant budgets and DESE final expenditure reports, by function code

## Paid outside the general fund

**Funds outside the voted budget spent $16,660,132 in four years: 13.5% of school spending in FY2026.**

- Spending outside the general fund was $4,387,961 in FY2023 and $4,004,476 in FY2026.
  - *not known:* Federal pandemic grants (ESSER) ended in FY2024; capital spending rose after. — closes: the district’s ESSER final expenditure reports
- Four years: fees and lunch $7,264,746, grants $6,050,464, the circuit breaker $1,797,214.
  - *not known:* Capital articles and other funds added $1,547,707; fees and lunch include gifts. — closes: the Town Meeting capital articles, FY2023–FY2026, by school account
- The largest single payee outside the general fund was THURSTON FOODS: $916,522.
  - *not known:* Invoices only. Pay runs and journal entries name no payee, and families paid for their own child are not named anywhere here. — closes: the accounts-payable detail behind each warrant, by fund

## Unspent money by fund

**Fees, lunch and the circuit breaker held $1,692,438 at the end of FY2023; by our count, $1,119,636 by FY2026.**

- These funds keep what they do not spend. School Choice held the most: $326,281 by our count.
  - *not known:* Our roll-forward: the town report’s FY2023 balance, plus every receipt, less every payment in the journal since. FY2026 orders still open are not taken off. — closes: the Town Accountant’s special revenue balances at 30 June 2026
- 9 of 12 funds tie to the town report to the cent for FY2023, receipts and spending both.
  - *not known:* 1 more ties once its interest, booked outside the school department, is added; 1 ties on the net; 1 does not: Greenthumb Revolving. — closes: the Town Accountant’s FY2023 detail for each school special revenue fund
- FY2023 and FY2024 grants were loaded with $1,868,592 of budget; $132,797 of it was never spent.
  - *not known:* Most grants are paid as they are spent, so an unspent award is usually money never drawn, not money held. — closes: DESE’s final expenditure report and carryover approval for each grant
  - *not known:* A loaded budget is not always the award: two FY2026 funds each carry a Title I budget, and one has spent nothing. — closes: DESE’s grant award notices for each school grant

## Grant spending by line

**Grant spending on a voted budget line went from 5.1% in FY2023 to 1.4% in FY2026.**

- The IDEA grants for FY2021 to FY2024 were booked to headings, never to a voted line.
  - *not known:* Their codes were 2300, 2400: teaching and instructional materials, but no single line. — closes: the IDEA grant budgets the district filed with DESE, by function code
- The FY2025 grant put $357,180 of its $394,801 on no function code at all.
  - *not known:* The FY2026 grant went to the heading 2000, instruction: $320,895. — closes: the business office’s account set-up for each grant
  - *hypothesis:* Why it changed is not in the ledger. A new account set-up, a new person, or a choice to code at the grant level all fit.
- Across every grant, $1,006,861 of $1,021,253 spent in FY2026 was on no line.
  - *not known:* The district’s End of Year report to the state puts its grant spending on function codes; this ledger mostly does not. — closes: the district’s End of Year Financial Report working papers, grant columns by function

## Special education budget, every fund

**Special education spending passed its voted budget every year, and other funds paid the difference.**

- Every fund spent $6,828,953 on special education in FY2026, against $6,073,840 voted.
  - *not known:* In FY2023 it was $5,335,622 against $4,543,293. FY2026 is not yet closed in this run. — closes: the Town’s journal report for FY2026, run after the year is closed
- The general fund itself came in under its vote every year, by $17,928 to $761,453.
- Other funds paid $773,041 to $1,065,546 a year on top: the circuit breaker and grants.
  - *hypothesis:* So outside money paid for more than the general fund budgeted, in every year. Whether the vote was set expecting it to is not in a ledger.
  - *not known:* Special education here is the accounts the ledger labels so; work paid from other accounts is not counted. — closes: the district’s End of Year Financial Report, special education program, all funds
